reviews.review:
I've tried to get into this game a few times because I usually love roguelites. I just can't. Every time I install the game, I play a dozen runs and just have to put it down because I'm having no fun. 

The characters move painfully slow. I've probably never played a game before where the baseline movement speed felt this bad. The game becomes much more playable with items like the Red Whip, which makes your character move significantly faster out of combat. It's too bad that's not the default. Is it ironic that a game all about being quick is hamstrung by its slow speed?

Then there's the combat. It starts out fine, but once I get past the first couple of levels, I feel that enemy health starts to spiral out of control. Keep in mind that this is on Rainstorm (normal) difficulty and on around medium on the difficulty bar (which is difficulty 3 out of 10). The game ends up either being "sit out of range of the enemy holding down the button for literally 60 seconds at a time" or "run away constantly, only stopping to fire that one ability you have that can hit multiple enemies".

I guess it comes down to this: this roguelite is the most item-reliant roguelite I've played. But this game's itemization is garbage. This isn't like The Binding of Isaac, which has incredible itemization while simultaneously being a game where you can salvage even the most terrible runs with pure skill. If you don't get the right item combination, there's virtually no hope. How many runs are YOU willing to tolerate before you find one that's actually fun?

Nice Gameplay combined with great soundtracks .... the game is highly addicting till the end.
The time pressure effect is pretty well integrated and keeps the game challenging, while you turn your char into a killing machine with several items.

One of the best action platformers out there!

What's not to love? This game has minor tweaks that could be made, but it is solid.

Where to start?

The first thing I noticed was the soundtrack. I instantly fell in love with the retro sound, yet it had a modern approach to it. Progressing through the stages feels in step with the music. 

The game itself is a blast. Collecting artifacts is key so you can mod the main game play and progress even further. Collecting powerups and stacking abilities is a fun aspect of this game that adds a lot of neat combinations to your attacks. 

Different classes of characters keep things different, though I must admin I still play primarly with the first character. 

The only thing I would want to see changed is the stacking for items you collect. For example the 56 Leaf Clover only provides max benefit at 8 stacks, so I would like to see the developer mark items as "max" if you have maxed the stack out.

I have not tried multiplayer yet, but I am sure it is just as amazing as single player. 

Love this game!
